notes.text: Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 173:18 together.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 48% of the team’s power-play time in 14 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 30% last season.
Matthew Robertson has not played this season.
Scott Morrow has not played this season.
Sean Durzi is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-four defenseman.
Luke Glendening was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Taylor Raddysh and Eeli Tolvanen.
James Reimer was added to the roster on Oct 26.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

NYR.head: The Rangers have a slight edge
NYR.body: Edmonton is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Hyman, while the Rangers have home-ice advantage. Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, though. Still, it’s close: the Oilers can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak. The Oilers have won two in a row, the last a 4-0 rout of the Islanders. Going in, the Oil are first in the Pacific (second in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th).
The Oilers’ record (.786) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.625), largely thanks to their finishing. The Rangers’ record (.536) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers (lowest) and the Rangers (2nd lowest) both lean hard on their top players. The Oilers have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Rangers, they forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 29 A / 37 P in 14 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 14 A / 26 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for ninth in the NHL.
Matt Tomkins is expected to start for Edmonton, his first start of the season, and Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) for the Rangers.
